strings.d1.s0.name: Naama Bay Beach
strings.d1.s0.tips: The heart of the resort, set in a bay: hotel beaches and house-reef snorkelling (northern end of the bay). Cooler in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Naama Bay Promenade
strings.d1.s1.tips: A pedestrian promenade with cafés, shisha and shops where you can haggle.
strings.d1.s2.name: Fares Seafood Naama
strings.d1.s2.tips: Sharm's best-known seafood: pick from the counter, priced by the kilo. Try the Sinai calamari.
strings.d1.s3.name: Hotel Pool / Siesta
strings.d1.s3.tips: It's 24°C in winter, so stay by the shore. The sea is 22°C.
strings.d1.s4.name: SOHO Square
strings.d1.s4.tips: Dancing fountain, ice bar and Culturama: the place for an evening out.
strings.d1.b0.name: El Masrien Grill Naama
strings.d1.b0.tips: Egyptian grill with kofta and chicken, a local favourite.
strings.d1.b1.name: Sharm Old Market
strings.d1.b1.tips: The old market: spices, papyrus and haggling, plus the Al Sahaba Mosque (lit up at night).
strings.d2.s0.name: Ras Mohammed National Park
strings.d2.s0.tips: At the tip of Sinai (30 minutes by boat or car). One of the world's best diving and snorkelling spots. Park fee about 15 USD.
strings.d2.s1.name: Shark Reef & Yolanda Reef
strings.d2.s1.tips: Wall reefs with Napoleon wrasse and barracuda, plus the toilets from the wrecked Yolanda.
strings.d2.s2.name: Mangrove Channel & Enchanted Lagoon
strings.d2.s2.tips: A mangrove channel and a salty "magic lake" formed by an earthquake.
strings.d2.s3.name: Lunch on the Boat
strings.d2.s3.tips: Included in the tour: grilled fish and rice.
strings.d2.s4.name: Marsa Bareika Bay
strings.d2.s4.tips: A calm bay for snorkelling and the beach. Return at 16:00.
strings.d2.b0.name: Ras Um Sid Reef
strings.d2.b0.tips: A headland reef within the city (Hadaba). If you have no boat, enjoy the view from Farsha Café.
strings.d2.b1.name: Farsha Café Ras Um Sid
strings.d2.b1.tips: A clifftop café with Bedouin rugs: sunset and shisha.
strings.d3.s0.name: Mount Sinai Night Climb
strings.d3.s0.tips: 3 hours from Sharm (tour leaves at 22:00). Moses' Ten Commandments mountain, 2,285 m: camel path plus 750 steps, sunrise, -5°C in winter, so wear a heavy coat.
strings.d3.s1.name: Summit Chapel at Sunrise
strings.d3.s1.tips: The Holy Trinity chapel, as Sinai's red mountains light up.
strings.d3.s2.name: Steps of Repentance Descent
strings.d3.s2.tips: 3,750 steps of the monks' path (Elijah's Basin). Watch your knees.
strings.d3.s3.name: Saint Catherine's Monastery
strings.d3.s3.tips: A 6th-century UNESCO monastery (the world's oldest working monastery): the Burning Bush, Moses' Well and icons. It may be closed on Fridays and Sundays.
strings.d3.s4.name: Bedouin Breakfast in St Catherine Village
strings.d3.s4.tips: Tea, bread and honey in a Bedouin tent. Return at 15:00 (afternoon nap).
strings.d3.b0.name: Dahab Blue Hole
strings.d3.b0.tips: Instead of Sinai: snorkel at Dahab's legendary 100 m blue hole (Bells), a hippie town, 1.5 hours away.
strings.d3.b1.name: Fox Camp St Catherine
strings.d4.s0.name: Tiran Island Boat Trip
strings.d4.s0.tips: 1 hour by boat from Sharm (tour about 50 USD). The island at the mouth of the Gulf of Aqaba has 4 reefs (Jackson, Woodhouse, Thomas, Gordon).
strings.d4.s1.name: Jackson Reef Snorkelling
strings.d4.s1.tips: A colourful coral garden with turtles and the wrecked Lara.
strings.d4.s2.name: Lunch on the Boat at Tiran
strings.d4.s3.name: Gordon Reef Swim
strings.d4.s3.tips: A shallow coral plateau where the Loullia wreck is visible. Return at 15:30.
strings.d4.s4.name: Naama Bay Sunset Walk
strings.d4.s4.tips: Promenade and sea in the evening.
strings.d4.b0.name: White Island
strings.d4.b0.tips: A sandbar island that appears at low tide. An alternative to the Ras Mohammed tour.
strings.d4.b1.name: Camel Bar Naama
strings.d4.b1.tips: The rooftop bar of Camel Dive Club: chat with the divers.
strings.d5.s0.name: Wadi Mandar Quad Safari
strings.d5.s0.tips: 1.5 hours by ATV/quad in the Sinai desert. Expect dust, so bring goggles.
strings.d5.s1.name: Bedouin Village Visit
strings.d5.s1.tips: Bedouin tea and bread baking, plus a short camel ride.
strings.d5.s2.name: Hotel Lunch & Siesta
strings.d5.s2.tips: Escape the midday heat with the pool and lunch.
strings.d5.s3.name: Desert Sunset & Stargazing Tour
strings.d5.s3.tips: Camels, a Bedouin dinner and stars through a telescope (no light pollution). Tour.
strings.d5.b0.name: Colored Canyon Nuweiba
strings.d5.b0.tips: A walk through a colourful rock canyon (2.5 hours' drive). A full day instead of the safari.
strings.d5.b1.name: Bedouin Dinner Camp
strings.d5.b1.tips: Lamb and rice, included in the tour.
strings.d6.s0.name: Discover Scuba Diving Naama
strings.d6.s0.tips: A trial dive (no certificate needed, 12 m with an instructor). Camel/Emperor Divers; Red Sea visibility 30 m.
strings.d6.s1.name: Lunch at the Dive Centre Café
strings.d6.s2.name: Sharm Aquarium / Old Market
strings.d6.s2.tips: In the afternoon, the market and Al Sahaba Mosque. Haggle.
strings.d6.s3.name: Al Fanar Ras Um Sid
strings.d6.s3.tips: Italian cuisine and seafood on the cliff, with the lighthouse and sunset.
strings.d6.b0.name: Dahab Lighthouse Reef & Town
strings.d6.b0.tips: A Dahab day: snorkel at Lighthouse and visit the seafront cafés, 1.5 hours away.
strings.d6.b1.name: Hard Rock Cafe Naama
strings.d6.b1.tips: An evening alternative with live music.
strings.d7.theme: Last swim and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Shark's Bay
strings.d7.s0.tips: A bay near the airport with a house reef and jetty. Your last swim.
strings.d7.s1.name: Hotel Breakfast
strings.d7.s1.tips: A long breakfast. Keep your cabin bag with you.
strings.d7.s2.name: Sharm Old Market
strings.d7.s3.name: Sharm El Sheikh International Airport
strings.d7.b0.name: Il Mercato Hadaba
strings.d7.b0.tips: An open-air mall, instead of the market.
strings.d7.b1.name: Tam Tam Naama
strings.d7.b1.tips: Egyptian breakfast: ful (fava bean stew) and taameya (falafel).
strings.note0: Haggle for taxis (Naama to Old Market 100-150 EGP) or use the hotel shuttle; Uber/Careem are limited. The airport is 15 minutes away. Tours leave from your hotel (Ras Mohammed, Tiran, Sinai, safari).
strings.note1: November to March is sunny at 22-25°C (Europe's winter refuge), the sea is 21-23°C and nights are cool. The Sinai summit can hit -5°C with snow in winter. January is the busiest month.
strings.note2: Sinai visa: a free 15-day "Sinai only" stamp covers Sharm, Dahab and Sinai alone; you can't go on to Cairo. Turkish citizens can get an e-visa or a visa on arrival for 25 USD.
strings.note3: Tour prices in USD: Ras Mohammed 40-60, Tiran 50, Sinai 40, safari 35-60, trial dive 90. Restaurants 200-400 EGP; tip 20-50 EGP everywhere.
strings.note4: Don't step on the coral: it's banned and fined. Use reef-friendly sun cream and bring water shoes. Women can dress casually in the resort, but cover up in the Old Market.
strings.note5: Sinai calamari, Egyptian breakfast (ful, taameya), koshari and umm ali dessert. Alcohol is served in hotels.
